data.long_meaning: From the Latin word 'lucus', meaning 'light'. In Christian tradition, the name Lucianor can symbolize the light of Christ shining within an individual. The name Lucianor carries the meaning “Light, shining one” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Latin. Parents who choose Lucianor usually hope their child will grow to embody light, shining one and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the inner light of Christ.
data.etymology: Lucianor belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Light, shining one.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Lucianor total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_hebrew.name: לוקיאנור
in_hebrew.long_meaning: לוקיאנור הוא שם המשלב את השמות לוקוס ויאנור, שמקורם ביוונית ובלטינית. לוקוס משמעותו 'אור' ויאנור קשור לשם יוחנן, שפירושו 'אלוהים הוא חנון'. לכן, לוקיאנור יכול להתפרש כ'נושא אור וקרינה מאלוהים' או 'מי שמביא את האור והחסד האלוהי'. השם לוקיאנור אינו מופיע ישירות בכתבי הקודש העבריים, אך הוא קשור למושגים של אור ותקווה, המופיעים לאורך התנך.

in_greek.name: Λουκιανός
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Λουκιανός είναι όνομα που συνδυάζει το Λουκος, που σημαίνει 'φως', και το Ιανός, που σχετίζεται με το Ιωάννης, που σημαίνει 'ο Θεός είναι χαριτωμένος'. Επομένως, ο Λουκιανός μπορεί να ερμηνευτεί ως 'εκείνος που φέρει φως και χάριν' ή 'ο φορέας του θείου φωτός και της χάριτος'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, παρόλο που δεν υπάρχει άμεση αναφορά στο όνομα Λουκιανός, οι έννοιες του φωτός και της χάριτος είναι κεντρικές στο μήνυμα του Χριστιανισμού.

in_latin.name: Lucianor
in_latin.long_meaning: Lucianor est nomen quod componitur ex Lucio, quod significat 'lux', et Ianor, quod refertur ad Ioannes, cuius significatio est 'Deus est gratiosus'. Quapropter, Lucianor interpretari potest ut 'ille qui fert lucem et gratiam Dei' vel 'portator lucis et favoris divini'. In primitiva Ecclesia Christiana, conceptus lucis et gratiae Dei fundamentales erant in doctrina Christiana.

in_english.name: Lucianor
in_english.meaning: Bringer of Light and Divine Grace
in_english.long_meaning: The name Lucianor is derived from the Latin words 'lux', meaning light, and 'Ianor', related to John, meaning 'God is gracious'. Therefore, Lucianor can be interpreted as 'Bringer of Light and Divine Grace' or 'Bearer of God's Light and Favor'. Although not directly mentioned in the Bible, the concepts of light and divine grace are central to Christian teachings. Historically, the name Lucianor has been used in Christian traditions to signify a person who brings spiritual enlightenment and grace.

data.cultural_impact: Lucianor is a name that carries a rich cultural background, derived from the Latin word 'lucus', meaning 'light'. Lucianor may have originated from ancient Rome where 'lucus' represented a sacred grove or particularly sunny place. The name also shares connections with St. Lucian of Antioch, a Christian martyr commemorated on February 13th, who was known for his radiant faith and extreme devotion to Christ. In history, individuals bearing this name have been associated with enlightenment, illumination, and purity.
data.spiritual_significance: Lucianor can represent the light of Christ shining within an individual. In the spiritual context, this name can serve as a constant reminder of the inner illumination that comes from embracing the Word of God. In his book "The Imitation of Christ," Thomas à Kempis encourages readers to "seek not thine own, but Christ's people, seeking not thine own will, but Christ's, and He shall be thine and thou shalt be His." Inhaling the spiritual significance of the name Lucianor reaffirms believers' commitment to surrendering ego and illumining their souls through encouragement, love, and devotion towards God, allowing Christ's light to reflect from within them.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Lucianor: The radiant light of Christ illuminating the darkest corners of the soul.

historical_references.reference: Lucianor was a name given to the son of Constantine the Great, who ruled as emperor from 306 to 337 AD. He was one of Constantine's four legitimate sons, and was given the name Lucianor in honor of his mother Flavia Iulia Constantia. However, he was not known to have ruled as emperor himself.

Another Lucianor is mentioned in the 'Historia de Preziosissima Sangue di Gesu Christo' or 'History of the Most Precious Blood of Jesus Christ', an anonymous work written in 1390 AD. In this work, Lucianor is described as a knight from the region of Tuscany, who was known for his devotion to the Eucharist and for his miraculous abilities to revive the dead. He was also said to have been granted the gift of perpetual youth by God.
